foliage.note: the envelope proven on the z1 pine 2026-08-19 (calm floor 0.07 for 60% of an 8s loop, seam 0.079, leakage 0.00). Ryan's brief: foliage NOT constantly moving -- little gusts blow through. | 2026-08-20 rebuilt on foliage-motion (cut-out cards over a clean plate). swing/flutter are UNVERIFIED pending Ryan's verdict on AB-CUTOUT-VS-WARP; the ROUTE is what changed. | swing 15->6 and flutter 0.35->0.15 on 2026-08-20 AFTER the compositor was fixed: the earlier 15 was chosen against a rig that was deleting 54% of the canopy, so it was compensating for missing paint rather than describing wind. Ink loss at 6 deg is 1.8%. | 2026-08-21 branchRadius 5 / attachMax 14: cards hinge WHERE THEY JOIN A BRANCH (knowledge/hinge-at-the-attachment.md). Ryan's verdict on evidence-attachment-pivot.png: radius 5 on the pine, swing as is. Then measured across all seven near trees (evidence-branch-radius-sweep.json, evidence-stroke-width-z3w.json): a fixed 5 hinged 1 of 68 big-canopy cards, because the other trees are drawn smaller and their branch strokes are thinner. branchRadius auto = branchRatio 0.55 x each tree's own p99 stroke half-width; 0.55 reproduces Ryan's 5 on the pine (9.17px) and gives 2-3 on the rest. | 2026-08-21 semantic:false FOR NOW. segment-semantic.py (CLIPSeg) masks are built for every z3w region and the tool reads them, but measured against the colour gate they are not yet trustworthy at this scale: in veto mode the model calls the whole orange maple in s-gorge-foreground 'bare grey rock' (19,014 ink px vetoed vs the colour gate's 6,063), and in keep mode it loses real crowns (pine 21 cards -> 16). See knowledge/perception-needs-a-boundary-model-too.md -- the missing link is SAM refining the model's boxes into exact masks. Flip this to true when that lands. | 2026-08-21 swing 6->12: Ryan's verdict on LADDER-pinebridge.mp4 (6/12/20 deg), his word was "12". At 6 deg tip travel was 7-12 screen px, about 0.5% of frame width. | 2026-08-21 leafMarks:true -- SECONDARY ACTION. Ryan: "I see the entire leaf structure is one green blob... make the individual leaves kind of twinkle and shake. move around leaf not entire tree." A card is a connected component of ink, so a spray whose leaf marks touch is ONE rigid blob on one hinge, and a blob on a hinge can only tilt. Each card is now split into its leaf marks by distance-transform watershed (seed spacing read from the ink's own median distance-transform value, so a distant tree with smaller marks still splits), and each mark rotates markSwing deg about its own centroid, narrows by markTwinkle as it turns edge-on, and jitters markShift px -- all on its own phase at markRate x the gust, composed with the card hinge as ONE affine so each leaf is resampled once. Measured on s-pine-over-bridge: 433 marks from 21 cards, +0 cost (4.5s for both halves of the A/B). | 2026-08-21 leafMarks BACK TO FALSE, same day it was added. Ryan, seeing it in the reel: "This new method of cutting out the leaves is a little too aggressive. It deforms the aesthetic. What we had before was actually looking good. I think if we just cut out little chunks, bushels of branches, and wave those around, like how we were doing before, that's a better method." The mechanism: a CARD moves the drawing rigidly, so every brushstroke arrives at the new position unchanged. Per-mark rotation and edge-on narrowing deform each stroke individually -- that is not animating the painting, it is redrawing it. Swing 12 stands; the card decomposition (a spray = a bushel of branches) stands. See knowledge/rigid-cards-preserve-the-brushwork.md. | 2026-08-21 swing BACK TO 6. Ryan on the v4 reel: 'Unfortunately, the leaves looked better before.' The ladder verdict of 12 was taken on ONE tight hold of ONE tree (LADDER-pinebridge); the reel spans fov 1.0 to 1.6 across seven trees, and 12 that read as lively in a tight hold reads as too much in a wide one. An amplitude chosen at one framing does not transfer to a film that changes framing. See knowledge/leaf-travel-is-measured-on-screen.md.

still.note: DELIBERATELY STILL, 2026-08-20. Ryan: "Just the ones you can see the leaves of… Not the mountains or the distant pine trees that are barely nubs." A nub has no delicate part -- it is a silhouette, and swinging a silhouette reads as the mountain deforming, which is the summit lesson one notch closer. Authored per region because NO statistic separates these from the near trees: mark count, mark size and ink fraction all put s-compound-canopies with s-great-trees-upper. Wang Meng was not drawing them differently, he was drawing them smaller. evidence: living/evidence-which-canopies-have-leaves.png
